She also competed on ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]''. In ''Big Brother 12 (US)'', Rachel a strong and outspoken competitor, quickly forming a showmance with [[Brendon Villegas]] and becoming an early target of [[The Brigade]] due to her overbearing personality. After Hayden nominated them in the first week, Brendon won the Power of Veto and saved himself, allowing Rachel to avoid eviction as [[Annie Whittington]] was sent home instead. Rachel won two early Head of Household competitions, using her first HOH to evict [[Monet Stunson]] and later targeting [[Hayden Moss]] and [[Kristen Bitting]], which exposed tension between her and the house. Despite her competition ability and loyalty to Brendon, Rachel struggled socially and was repeatedly viewed as a threat, especially by The Brigade. After [[Matt Hoffman]] nominated Rachel and Brendon during his HOH in Week 5, she fought to stay. However, when [[Britney Haynes]] won the Power of Veto and chose not to use it, Rachel was unanimously evicted on Day 41 for being seen as the more significant threat of the duo. She placed 9th and was the first member of the [[jury]]. She would cast her jury vote for [[Lane Elenburg]], feeling he had played the best social game. She returned to the game in ''Big Brother 13 (US)'' as part of the [[Dynamic Duos|dynamic duo]] twist, being partnered with her then fiancé, now husband, Brendon Villegas. Rachel immediately established herself as a major threat by winning two Head of Household competitions early on and leading the [[Veterans]] alliance after [[Dick Donato]] walked from the game. After the Veterans alliance fractured due to [[Daniele Briones|Daniele Briones']] attempt to backdoor fellow veterans [[Jeff Schroeder]] and [[Jordan Lloyd]], Rachel became a target and was nominated alongside Brendon by Daniele in Week 4; Brendon saved her with the Power of Veto but was evicted. Rachel survived the block in Week 5 and Brendon returned through a battle back twist, but he was soon evicted again, leaving her and the remaining veterans vulnerable. She survived a double eviction that sent Jeff out, then won the final five HoH and used her position to eliminate [[Kalia Booker]]. After reaching the Final 3 with [[Porsche Briggs]] and [[Adam Poch]], Rachel won the final HoH, evicted Adam, and defeated Porsche 4-3 in the jury vote to win the $500,000 grand prize, completing a comeback victory after being targeted throughout the game. In ''Big Brother 27 (US)'', Rachel was the sole returning player and her presence dominated the first half of the season. Throughout her time in the game, she made tight bonds with [[Amy Bingham]], [[Ashley Hollis]], and [[Jimmy Heagerty]], while also developing season-long rivalries with [[Keanu Soto]] and [[Vince Panaro]]. Despite her massive target, Rachel managed to avoid being nominated during her time in the house by insulating herself well and being used as a shield by other players. Unfortunately for Rachel, her luck ran out when she failed to complete the [[Hit The Road]] competition in the allotted time at the White Locust Resort, resulting in her abrupt exit from the game on Day 60 and becoming the first member of the jury. Rachel's exit this season was the source of much controversy, especially since she managed to avoid being nominated up to that point in the game. Despite her constant irritation to other houseguests and viewers often due to her grating laugh and frequent crying, she and Brendon ("Brenchel") developed a huge fan base. Due to her competition prowess, she is considered one of the greatest physical players in the show's history, having won every endurance competition she has competed in.

Known for his affable personality and uxorious nature, Will played a quiet yet effective game. Will found himself as a frequent [[pawn]] early on but was able to solidify several key bonds, primarily acting as the father figure to [[Ava Pearl]] and [[Ashley Hollis]] on veteran [[Rachel Reilly]]'s side of the house. His likable and down-to-earth presence kept him safe and landed him in several alliances (most notably [[The Judges]]) during the pre-[[The Jury|jury]]. Nominated in Week 9 alongside Ashley, the latter pressured [[Vince Panaro]] and [[Morgan Pope]] to keep her over him in spite of his low physical threat level due to his perceived likability and Ashley's utility. Will was thus evicted by a 3-2 vote, placing 8th and becoming the second juror.

[[Zae Frederich]] |HOHs = 0 |Nominations = 1 (Week 5) |Vetos = 0 |Blockbuster = 0 |Days = 38 |OtherPrizes = $10,000 |InstagramUserName = zcorn_29 }}'''Zachary Senot "Zach" Cornell''' was a houseguest on ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]''. After winning the [[Secret Power Competition|BB Buy Off]] power on Day 1, Zach led the house's social dynamics alongside close ally [[Vince Panaro]], but they were soon put in jeopardy after not flipping the Week 3 eviction vote. Though remaining in a powerful position after forming [[The Melting Pot|an alliance]] with Week 4 [[Head of Household|HOH]] [[Mickey Lee]], [[Morgan Pope]], and Vince, he was a last minute nomination by Week 5 HOH [[Ava Pearl]], and subsequently chose not to give up his $10,000 that came with the BB Buy Off power, in supposed fear that Morgan would be his replacement. After primary target [[Keanu Soto]] won the [[Second Chance Challenge|Block Buster]], Zach was evicted by an 8-2 vote over Vince for his high social threat level, placing 13th. Upon his eviction, [[Julie Chen-Moonves]] playfully tapped Zach on the head with her cards for getting evicted with the power in his possession.
